key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that a domain-tuned retrieval-augmented generator can deliver correct, pedagogically useful explanations for abstract theoretical computer science topics that are hard to teach with standard static resources.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical blueprint for building educational AI systems for proof-heavy STEM domains by combining curated knowledge bases, notation-aware retrieval, and teaching-oriented reranking.
method: Built a TCS-specific RAG system over textbooks, lecture slides, solved problems, proof templates, and worksheets.
Added mathematical entity recognition, notation-aware retrieval, and pedagogical reranking to improve answer quality.
Evaluated on 179 exam-style questions across core algorithm-analysis and complexity topics.
evidence_signal: On 179 curated questions, AlgoRAG achieved a 100% success rate with 38.0 s mean response time; despite BLEU-4 being zero, it reached ROUGE-1 F1 of 0.0963, ROUGE-L F1 of 0.0683, and pedagogical quality of 0.7620.
watch_item: Zero BLEU-4 highlights that n-gram metrics can miss mathematically equivalent proofs, so human or rubric-based evaluation is important.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
